title: 3 Nights in Dallas — A Family Visit Itinerary: BBQ, Arts & Plano Homecoming
description: A personalized 3-night Dallas/Plano itinerary for a family visit — Pecan Lodge BBQ, Dallas Arts District, Deep Ellum, Fort Worth Stockyards, and the best Vietnamese food in Plano.

days.title: Arrive, Settle In & Plano Homecoming
days.description: No need to rush into Dallas today. You're home. Settle in at your parents' place, catch up over tea, then explore the surprisingly great food and shopping scene right in Plano. Save the big Dallas day for tomorrow.

activities.name: DFW Airport → Plano
activities.description: From DFW Airport: ~30 min drive north via TX-121 / Dallas North Tollway. If your parents are picking you up, perfect. If renting a car, grab one at the airport — you'll need it all trip. From Love Field: ~35 min via US-75 North. Drop your bags, hug your parents, drink whatever they hand you. The city can wait.
tips: If you're arriving early and your parents aren't ready, Legacy Hall food hall in Legacy West is a great place to kill time with coffee and snacks while you wait.

activities.name: Legacy West & Shops at Legacy
activities.description: A beautiful open-air shopping and dining complex right in Plano. This isn't a suburban strip mall — it's genuinely nice. Walk around, browse the shops, get coffee at Ascension Coffee (excellent pour-overs and pastries), or just sit on the patio and people-watch in the Texas sunshine. The Shops at Legacy next door has a more neighborhood-bar vibe with restaurants and patios lining Legacy Drive. Great for a late afternoon drink.
details: 📍 Legacy West: 7800 Windrose Ave, Plano · Shops at Legacy: Legacy Dr & Bishop Rd · Free to walk around

days.neighborhoods: Dallas Arts District · Deep Ellum · Bishop Arts
days.title: Dallas Arts, Legendary BBQ & Live Music
days.description: Today you explore Dallas proper. World-class museums in the morning, the best BBQ in Texas for lunch, and Deep Ellum's murals and live music at night. This is the big Dallas day — but still relaxed. Pick what excites you and skip the rest.

activities.name: Dallas Arts District
activities.description: The largest contiguous urban arts district in the US. Start with the Dallas Museum of Art — it's free and has a world-class collection spanning 5,000 years. The building itself is beautiful. Spend 1–2 hours here, focusing on whatever catches your eye. Don't try to see everything. If science is more your speed, the Perot Museum of Nature and Science is right nearby — a stunning building designed by Thom Mayne with incredible interactive exhibits. Great if your parents come along.
details: 📍 Dallas Museum of Art: 1717 N Harwood St · Free · 11am–5pm Sun
📍 Perot Museum: 2201 N Field St · $22 adults · 10am–5pm
tips: The Klyde Warren Park sits right between the Arts District and Uptown — a beautiful deck park built over a freeway. Food trucks line the south edge on weekends. Great for a morning stroll or coffee break between museums.

activities.name: Deep Ellum — Dallas's Creative Heart
activities.description: You're already here for BBQ, so walk it off. Deep Ellum is Dallas's most vibrant neighborhood — every wall is covered in murals, there are vinyl shops and vintage stores on every block, and the energy is infectious even during the day. Walk down Main Street and Elm Street just taking in the street art. Stop into Josey Records if you're into vinyl — it's massive and wonderfully curated. Deep Ellum Brewing Company has a great taproom if you want a post-BBQ beer.
details: 📍 Deep Ellum: Main St & Elm St between Good Latimer & Hall St · Free to explore

activities.name: Reunion Tower GeO-Deck
activities.description: The iconic ball-topped tower on the Dallas skyline. The observation deck gives you 360° views of the whole DFW metroplex. Come in late afternoon to catch the city in golden light transitioning to sunset. On a clear day you can see forever — the flat Texas landscape means the view stretches to the horizon in every direction.

activities.name: Bishop Arts District
activities.description: Head south to Bishop Arts for dinner and evening vibes. This charming neighborhood in Oak Cliff is full of independent boutiques, galleries, and excellent restaurants all within a few walkable blocks. It's the anti-suburban Dallas — eclectic, artsy, and full of character. After dinner, walk around Bishop Arts. Grab a drink at The Foundry (cocktails) or Bishop Cider Co. (Texas ciders on tap). If you're up for it, head back to Deep Ellum for live music — Trees, The Bomb Factory, or just bar-hop along Elm Street. Something's always playing.

days.neighborhoods: Fort Worth Stockyards · Sundance Square · Carrollton
days.title: Fort Worth Day Trip & Korean BBQ Night
days.description: Fort Worth is the cultural counterweight to Dallas — cowboy heritage, Western art, and a genuinely different vibe that's only 45 minutes away. Then come back for Korean BBQ in Carrollton, because DFW's Korean food scene is absurdly good.

activities.name: Fort Worth Stockyards
activities.description: The Stockyards are the real deal — a National Historic District where the Old West isn't a theme park, it's just... the neighborhood. Brick streets, saloons, leather shops, and cowboys in boots who actually work ranches. Come by 11:30am to catch the daily cattle drive — real Texas longhorns herded down Exchange Avenue by mounted cowboys. It's free and genuinely cool. Walk down Exchange Avenue and poke into the shops. M.L. Leddy's for custom boots (window shopping is free), Stockyards Station for Western goods and souvenirs. The whole district has a warm, authentic energy that Dallas doesn't try to replicate.
details: 📍 130 E Exchange Ave, Fort Worth · Free to walk around · Cattle drive at 11:30am & 4:00pm daily

activities.name: Sundance Square & Fort Worth Cultural District
activities.description: After lunch, drive to Sundance Square in downtown Fort Worth — a beautiful pedestrian-friendly plaza surrounded by restaurants and shops. It's a nice spot to walk and grab coffee. If you have time and energy, Fort Worth's museum district is world-class: the Kimbell Art Museum (Louis Kahn's masterpiece building, free for the permanent collection) and the Modern Art Museum of Fort Worth (Tadao Ando's gorgeous concrete-and-water building) are both architectural landmarks worth visiting even if you're not a museum person. Pick one — don't try to do both unless you're really into it.
details: 📍 Kimbell: 3333 Camp Bowie Blvd · Free (permanent collection) · Closed Mon
tips: The drive back from Fort Worth to Plano takes about 45 min–1 hr depending on traffic. Leave by 4pm to avoid the worst of I-30/I-35W rush hour.

days.title: Last Morning in Plano & Heading Home
days.description: A gentle final morning. No rushing. Enjoy a last meal with the family, stock up on Asian groceries if you want, and head to the airport with a full heart and a fuller stomach.

activities.name: 99 Ranch Market Area
activities.description: If you have time before your flight, swing by the 99 Ranch Market area on Legacy Drive — it's an Asian grocery wonderland. Stock up on snacks, sauces, and anything you can't get back home. The food court inside has solid quick bites. 85°C Bakery Cafe next door makes incredible sea salt coffee and fresh-baked bread that's perfect for the road (or the plane). The whole area around here — H Mart, various Chinese bakeries, boba shops — is Plano's Asian food corridor at its finest. Your parents probably know all the secrets here.
details: 📍 99 Ranch: 3100 Independence Pkwy, Plano · 85°C: same shopping center

activities.name: Head to the Airport
activities.description: Allow 45 min–1 hr to get from Plano to DFW Airport (more during rush hour). If you have time to kill at the airport, Terminal D has the best food options. Say bye to your parents, promise to come back soon, and actually mean it this time.
tips: If you stocked up at 99 Ranch, double-check TSA rules for what you can carry on. Most dry goods and sealed sauces are fine in checked bags. Fresh produce may not be worth the hassle.

days.title: 🍜 DFW Food Guide — Beyond the Itinerary
days.description: DFW's food scene is massive and incredibly diverse. Here are extra recommendations organized by craving — swap any of these into the itinerary based on your mood.
